This Day, The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is filed under Section-173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for brevity) by the appellant-claimant, calling in question the judgment and award dated 24.03.2015, passed in M.V.C.No.4430/2010, on the file of the XX Additional Judge & XVIII ACMM,
Bengaluru, (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity) challenging the dismissal of the claim petition.

Brief facts:
2. On 23.05.2010, the claimant was driving a car bearing No.KA-05-C-2241 from Muthathi towards Bangalore and when he came near Ravugodlu Gate, on Sri.K.Nagarajachari vs M/S Fac Sri Ram Transport Finance on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67657795/
2 Kanakapura-Bangalore Road, at that time at about 4.15 p.m., the driver of the lorry bearing no.KA-02-D-1349 in high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, while coming from opposite direction, by overtaking another vehicle and dashed against the car.

sentences.text: As a result, the claimant of MVC No.4429/2010 sustained injuries and the car of the claimant in the present appeal was fully damaged.
3. Hence, a claim petition was filed by the appellant- claimant under Section-166 of the M.V. Act, claiming compensation for the damage of the car.
The Tribunal on appreciating the materials on record dismissed the claim petition.

4. Heard arguments of the learned counsel for the parties and perused the materials on record.
5.

The Tribunal has dismissed the claim petition on the ground that presuming itself that after getting repair of the car, the claimant has submitted the repair bills and receipts to the Future General Insurance Company and the said insurance company has reimbursed the entire repair charges.
6. This Court on an earlier occasion by passing an order in MFA No.8225/2012, dated 14.08.2014

,
remanded the case to the Tribunal for fresh consideration of the case by giving opportunity to adduce any further evidence regarding communication between the claimant and his insurer and whether the vehicle was lying idle, and whether the vehicle has got repaired or not and whether the vehicle is fit for repair or has to be put to scrap.
Therefore, with these observations, this Court has remanded this case to the Tribunal for fresh consideration.
7. After remand, the claimant got examined himself but has not examined any other witnesses and produced Exhibits-P73 and P74.
Exhibit-P73 is a letter and Exhibit-P74 is car fitness certificate showing that the car was idle and has become scrap.
It is the evidence of the claimant that he has not got repaired the vehicle as he had no money to pay the repair, which costs around Rs.6 to 7 lakhs.
Therefore, he could not repair the vehicle.
Therefore, the vehicle was lying idle in the garage.
Exhibit-P16 is the letter issued by the Future General Insurance Company and it is stated that the claim of the claimant was closed without payment on account of non- submissions of the documents.
The Authorized Officer of the said insurance company is to be examined, is the rule of evidence.
Just because the owner of the company or the authorized representative of the insurance company is not examined, that cannot be made a ground to reject Exhibit- P16.
Exhibit-P16 is found to be believable that can be relied.
8. It is not the contention of the respondent - insurance company that Exhibit-P16 is concocted document.
Therefore, just because of non-examination of the owner or authorized representative of the Future General Insurance Company, cannot be a ground to reject the documentary evidence.
Therefore, it is proved that the claimant has not received any amount from Future General Insurance Company, which is claimant's vehicle insurer.
The claimant has not submitted documents to his insurer because the claimant has not got repaired his vehicle.
Therefore, there is no question of generating bills, invoices bills and receipts.

Therefore, the claimant has not received any amount Sri.K.Nagarajachari vs M/S Fac Sri Ram Transport Finance on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67657795/
3 of compensation from his insurer.

sentences.text: 9. Exhibits-P38 to P64 are the photographs produced before the Tribunal before remanding the case at the first instance before the Tribunal, which shows that the vehicle Toyoto Qualis has almost become scrap vehicle and is not fit for repair.

Exhibit-P73 is the letter issued by the Toyota Nandi that the claimant had taken the vehicle back by paying estimation and parking charges without pressing for the insurance company i.e., the Future General Insurance Company.

Therefore, the claimant is not able to process for the insurance company from the insurer because the claimant has not got repaired, as it is not feasible to get repaired by spending huge amount as estimated by the Surveyor and as estimated by the Toyota Company.
Therefore, it is proved that the claimant has not got amount from the insurer that is from the Future General Insurance Company.
10. Exhibit-P74 are photographs which are produced after remanding the case that the vehicle has become completely scrap and not fit for repair.
Therefore, just because the owner or any authorized person of the garage has not been examined, that cannot be a ground to say that the vehicle has not become scrap.
Examination of the witness in support of the document is a mere rule of evidence.
If documents inspire confidence before the Court that could be considered even without examining the employer / authorized representative of the company.
The evidence produced in the claim proceedings before the Tribunal are to be considered on the principle of preponderance of probabilities, but not adopting the theory of beyond reasonable doubt.

What would be the probability involved in the case is whether the vehicle was damaged extensively, rendering it unusable and has become scrap and whether the claimant has claimed compensation from its insurer, are to be ascertained by appreciating the evidence on record.

11. As discussed above on all its preponderance of probabilities it is proved that the vehicle has got damage in the accident extensively rendering unusable and become scrap and thus the vehicle has been kept idle.

Therefore, the presumption made by the Tribunal by drawing an adverse inference that the claimant might have got repaired and submitted bills and receipts and might have already obtained compensation from Future General Insurance Company is not correct.
This presumption made by the Tribunal is completely perverse and contrary to law.
Therefore, it is proved that there is no repair carried out to the vehicle and the vehicle is kept idle and has become scrap.
12. PW-3 is the Valued Surveyor who has submitted his estimation.
He has surveyed the damaged car and as per his Survey Report he has assessed the repair cost - 10 - would be Rs.4,59,956/- and has produced documents in this regard, as per Exhibits-P35 and P37.
Exhibit-P35 is the license issued to PW-3 for surveying the vehicle.
Exhibit-P37 is the final survey report issued by PW-3.

PW-3 has assessed the total repair liability assessed as Rs.4,59,956/-
excluding the labour, towing charges, etc., and the cost of spare parts, labour, towing charges, etc.,
the surveyor has submitted a report of total estimation of repair as Rs.6,75,172/-.
But the claimant has not got repaired the vehicle.

Therefore, the labour charges and cost of spare parts are to be excluded and accordingly as per survey report, the net repair liability assessed as Rs.4,59,956/-, that Sri.K.Nagarajachari vs M/S Fac Sri Ram Transport Finance on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67657795/

sentences.text: 4 much amount the claimant is entitled.
Where such extensive damage involving huge repair cost, it is quite natural that the claimant would become reluctant to repair the vehicle.
Therefore, the vehicle was constrained to be kept idle.
Hence, the claimant has lost service of his vehicle.
Therefore, the damages are to be awarded.
Assuming there was no accident, then what - 11 - would have been the value of the vehicle as on the date of the accident if the accident had not occurred that would be granted.
13. Accordingly, as per the survey report the repair liability assessed is as Rs.4,59,956/-.

Therefore,
on this ground, the claimant is entitled for compensation from the respondent - insurance company.
Therefore, for the reasons discussed above dismissing the claim petition is unsustainable and accordingly set-aside.
Therefore, the appeal is liable to be allowed in part.

Hence, I pass the following order:
14.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.
ii. The impugned judgment and award dated 24.03.2015, passed in M.V.C.No.4430/2010, on - 12 - the file of the XX Additional Judge & XVIII ACMM, Bengaluru, is set-aside.

iv. The Respondent No.3 - insurance company  shall pay the compensation to the  appellant/claimant.
